To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) people are sensitive to the information value of comparison standards; (2) they are particularly sensitive to the diagnosticity of the standard; (3) they are less sensitive to the similarity of the standard; and (4) their sensitivity to diagnosticity is moderated by their need for cognition and by the perceived similarity of the target.

(a) the comparison process is not a unitary process but rather is comprised of two fundamentally different processes, namely, similarity testing and dissimilarity testing; and (b) similarity testing and dissimilarities testing lead to different outcomes in social judgment.

(a) similarity and dissimilarity testing are 2 fundamental processes that selectively activate target knowledge indicating target–comparison similarity and dissimiliarity, respectively, (b) similarity and dissimilarly testing have different consequences for target evaluation, and (c) the respective consequences are mediated by the selective accessibility of target knowledge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of comparisons in human judgment.
the processes by which individuals make social judgments and with the consequences of such processes for social behavior.
the processes and consequences of social comparison in judgment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the comparison processes in social judgment can have a variety of consequences.
comparison processes are ubiquitous in social judgment.
the comparison process has an effect on social judgment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more people are aware of their social comparison, the more they tend to compare, the less they like themselves, and the more they engage in self-improvement.
we have shown that the consequences of social comparison depend on the type of comparison process that is used to form the comparison.
we have shown that the way people compare themselves with other people has profound consequences for how they think and feel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the comparison process is not a simple one.
the comparison process can have a variety of consequences for subsequent judgments and decisions.
the comparison process is more complex than it may appear at first glance.
